newsitem.title: USA: Oil union rejects Tosco refinery contract.
newsitem.headline: Oil union rejects Tosco refinery contract.

text.p: Union representatives from four California refiners Tuesday rejected a contract offer made March 10 by Tosco Corp, leaving the plants' 900 union members waiting for a response from the company.

Tosco, a refiner based in Stamford, Conn., has been negotiating a new contract with the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers Union (O.C.A.W), whose members help run the four refineries now owned by Unocal Corp.
Tosco will acquire the plants and other downstream assets from Unocal March 31.
"We need to wait and see what their response to this rejection will be," Steve Sullivan, an O.C.A.W. representative told Reuters Wednesday.
A team of 17 union members from the refineries rejected Tosco's offer because it contained inadequate medical and pension plans, Sullivan said.
A Tosco executive declined comment on negotations but said he expected them to end amicably.
Sullivan said O.C.A.W's international president, Robert Wages, was also looking over the contract, but doubted the union chief will approve the terms.

Union officials have claimed that Tosco plans to cut up to 150 refinery jobs. But while support runs strong for a strike, Sullivan said he doubted that the union will walk out on April 1, the first day of Tosco's ownership.
"We're really not looking at striking at this point," he said.
